clue.text: In excruciating terminal pain, you said? That’s awkward

indicators.note: terminal means at the end, so only the last letter of excruciating is kept
said tells us to take the sound of the word you rather than its spelling
the spoken letter sits in the word for pain, wrapped by it

blocks.note: the final letter of excruciating
an ache is a dull pain
the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: Someone in agony mumbles something, and the listener finds the moment uncomfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: G, then U placed inside ACHE, gives GAUCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche is borrowed from French for left-handed and means socially clumsy or tactless.

clue.text: Be inappropriate with young Indian woman

blocks.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
describes the woman and supplies no letters of its own: a young woman is a miss
a miss is a girl or unmarried young woman

explanation.surface: A warning against behaving improperly towards a young woman from India.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian is read as a noun meaning something from India, here the state of Goa.
explanation.definitionFit: To go amiss is to turn out wrongly or be out of place, close to being unsuitable.

clue.text: Up to the point when circling crow flies off jauntily

indicators.note: a bird that flies off leaves, so the letters of the bird depart from the longer word they encircled

blocks.note: taken as written
a jay belongs to the crow family; its J and A open the word and its Y closes it, circling the rest

explanation.surface: A crow wheels round and then flaps away in a carefree manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove JA from the front and Y from the end of JAUNTILY to leave UNTIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Until is a conjunction or preposition meaning as far as a stated time and no longer.

clue.text: Head of household turned aghast seeing this on X (formerly Twitter)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of household is used
turned suggests the letters of the next word have been twisted into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of household
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent is horrified at what they spot on the social network X.
explanation.walkthrough: H followed by AGHAST rearranged gives HASHTAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hashtag is the pound-sign label used to tag topics in posts on that social media platform.

clue.text: Englishmen’s ball

blocks.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person, so two of them make Englishmen

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like a ball belonging to Englishmen, but the plural is just two Poms side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a small fluffy woollen ball used to decorate hats and other clothing.

clue.text: Wealthy East German first reality denier

indicators.note: first places the German word at the front, ahead of the word for wealthy

blocks.note: Ost is the German word for east
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A wealthy man from the former East Germany who refuses to face the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: East German looks like a description of a person from the GDR, but it means east in German.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is said to bury its head in the sand, so the name is used for anyone ignoring unwelcome facts.

clue.text: Soldier and poet to speak of birds

indicators.note: speaking of something here means saying it aloud, so we want the sound of the poet's name, not its spelling

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
John Keats, the Romantic poet

explanation.surface: A paratrooper and a poet are about to lecture on birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets are small long-tailed parrots, so they are a kind of bird.

clue.text: After thirty seconds, rave about goddess

indicators.note: after places the rearranged word behind the time unit
about suggests moving the letters around into another order

blocks.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and the first half of the word minute is these three letters
the letters of rave rearranged

explanation.surface: Thirty seconds in, someone starts gushing about a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Half a minute is literally half of the word minute; MIN plus ERVA gives MINERVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman deity of wisdom, crafts and strategy, counterpart of Greek Athena.

clue.text: King Edward dressed for dinner?

blocks.note: surface reading: a British monarch putting on formal clothes for an evening meal
setter's reading: King Edward is a popular British variety of spud, here served still in its skin

explanation.surface: The king changes into his evening wear before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety; the skin is the coat it is dressed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked spud served in its skin is said to wear a coat, so a King Edward cooked that way is clothed for the meal.

clue.text: Massive heart, cryptically?

blocks.note: surface reading: a large or enlarged heart
setter's reading: the answer, read as crossword instructions, says to scramble the letters of the planet's name, which gives the word heart

explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read cryptically is an instruction (planet name, shattered) whose result is the word heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something earth-shattering is momentous or enormous in importance, so massive in impact.

clue.text: In this country one permitted to get heart, liver or kidney

indicators.note: in puts the single numeral inside the abbreviation for the nation

blocks.note: this is a British paper, so this country is Great Britain
Roman numeral one
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A rule about who in Britain is allowed to receive a donated organ.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British newspaper, this country means Great Britain; the surface's transplant organs are the definition, not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Giblets are the edible internal organs of a bird, such as its heart, liver and gizzard.

clue.text: Footballers hogging the centre of attention? That’s pants!

indicators.note: centre points to the middle letter of attention
to hog is to keep something to yourself, so the players hold the letter inside them

blocks.note: footballers kick the ball
the fifth of nine letters in attention

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses footballers who crave the spotlight as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang pants means nonsense, and so does the exclamation knickers; knickers are also women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British exclamations of disbelief or contempt, meaning rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: East of France consuming load of this delicacy

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the French word swallows the word for load

blocks.note: est is French for east
cargo is a load carried by ship or plane

explanation.surface: Someone in eastern France tucks into a heap of a local delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: East of France means the French word for east, not a region of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked as a dish, a celebrated French delicacy usually served with garlic butter.

clue.text: An agricultural product and where it’s stashed up for the citadel

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a crop is what a farm produces
a silo is a tower for storing grain

explanation.surface: A farmer's harvest and its storage are turned into a hilltop fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: A + CROP + OLIS (SILO upwards) gives ACROPOLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is the fortified high part of an ancient Greek city, most famously in Athens.

clue.text: Keeps longing internally as they laugh

definitions.note: a pronoun clause standing for the plural noun

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the word for longing sits within the word for keeps

blocks.note: has means holds or keeps
a yen is a yearning

explanation.surface: Someone nurses a secret desire while others laugh at them.
explanation.walkthrough: Yen for a longing comes from a Chinese word, not the Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted hyenas are famous for a cackling call that sounds like human laughter.

clue.text: ‘Marine life law rejected by RSPC leader’ – The Guardian

indicators.note: rejected suggests something sent back, so the word is read the other way
the leader of a group of letters is the first one

blocks.note: law written backwards
first letter of RSPC
the clue appears in The Guardian, which can refer to itself as we or us

explanation.surface: A mock newspaper headline about a marine protection law being turned down by an animal charity's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The RSPCA is Britain's animal welfare charity; dropping its A makes RSPC look like it, though only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A walrus is a large tusked sea mammal of Arctic waters, an example of sea creatures.

clue.text: Supported by previous partners, woman getting extensions

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top, so the woman's name comes before the partners

blocks.note: a woman's name
exes are former spouses or partners

explanation.surface: A woman relies on her former partners to fund building work.
explanation.definitionFit: Annexes are buildings or rooms added on to a main building, so they are additions.

clue.text: Relative pace and quiet

blocks.note: a step is a pace
as in keep mum: say nothing

explanation.surface: Reads like a phrase about comparative speed and calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Relative looks like an adjective attached to pace, but it is a noun naming a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepmum is a father's wife who is not one's mother, a family member by marriage.

clue.text: Given a fine joke Philistine discarded

blocks.note: a pun is a play on words
Philistine is the setter, who refers to themselves as I
shed means cast off

explanation.surface: The setter's joke was binned and they were penalised for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Philistine is the name of this puzzle's setter, so it stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fined is a penalty, so someone given a fine has been penalised by a court.

clue.text: See 8
Business invested in gas supply primarily for right-wingers

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so the abbreviation goes inside the gas
primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of supply is used

blocks.note: neon is a noble gas
Co is the abbreviation for company
first letter of supply

explanation.surface: A firm puts money into gas provision mainly to please conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas suggests a utility supply, but here it is a specific element of the noble gases.
explanation.definitionFit: Neocons are neoconservatives, hawkish political figures on the American right.

clue.text: Eastenders pick up percussion through it

definitions.text: Eastenders pick up percussion through it

indicators.note: Cockney Londoners from the East End traditionally drop the h at the start of words

blocks.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, said without its opening h
a drum is a percussion instrument

explanation.surface: Fans of the TV soap catch the famous drum beats of its theme tune.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in East London, whose closing theme opens with drum beats; Cockneys say 'ear for hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the membrane in the ear that vibrates so people can detect sounds like drumming.

clue.text: Eats out after a brief rest: minute steak, fish ‘n’ chips or haute cuisine, for example

definitions.text: minute steak, fish ‘n’ chips or haute cuisine, for example

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order
after puts the rearranged letters behind the short rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a nap is a short sleep
the letters of eats rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats out after a short nap, choosing from steak, chippy food or fine dining.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu items are not food here: each is three syllables stressed on the last, like mi-nute STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: An anapaest is a metrical foot of two unstressed syllables then a stressed one, which each listed phrase illustrates.

clue.text: Awards for SUVs?

blocks.note: SUVs are big vehicles: outsize cars, with OS the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Imagines prizes being handed out to big four-by-fours.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the Academy Awards, the American film industry's annual prizes.

clue.text: Beast arrived and left

blocks.note: came means arrived
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An animal shows up and then goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert animal, a beast of burden.

clue.text: Income tax malarkey 75%? Ridiculous!

indicators.note: keeping three quarters of an eight-letter word means dropping its last two letters
something ridiculous is absurd and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the first six of its eight letters

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at a tax bill taking three quarters of one's income.
explanation.walkthrough: Ridiculous looks like part of the outburst, and the closing ! is itself the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol printed at the end of the clue is what this punctuation mark is called.

clue.text: Tennis score ends with indistinguishable seeds

indicators.note: ends points to the final letter of each of the two preceding words

blocks.note: the last letters of tennis and score
things that are the same cannot be told apart

explanation.surface: A tennis match finishes level, with the players' seedings impossible to separate.
explanation.walkthrough: Seeds suggests tennis seedings, but it is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a plant whose small oily seeds are scattered on bread and pressed for oil.

clue.text: My usual heartless chaotic refuge

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is taken away
chaotic means in disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the five-letter word with its central U removed

explanation.surface: Someone's normal heartless chaos finds them a safe haven.
explanation.walkthrough: MY plus USAL rearranged gives ASYLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or sanctuary, such as that granted by a state to a political refugee.
